content.text:
**Static sites travel well; the polished path is Cloudflare Workers.** Rough portability: **~6.5/10**.

### What works elsewhere
Sites are plain Astro static output (`dist/`). No SSR adapter, so you can put that folder on Vercel/Netlify static, S3+CDN, nginx, GitHub Pages, etc. Orso itself does not push to a CDN — publish is git merge → your repo’s CI.

Preview / “Open live site” work on **any** host if CI records a GitHub Deployment with `environment_url`. Local `orso serve` / the desktop daemon do not care where the site lives.

### Where Cloudflare is the default
The starter ships `wrangler.toml` + `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (Workers static assets, branch preview aliases). Live-URL fallbacks in the daemon assume Workers/`workers.dev` when Deployments are missing. Planned hosted product UI (`/app`) is also designed as a CF Worker.

### Friction on other methods
| Approach | Reality |
|---|---|
| Vercel / Netlify / S3 / self-host | Possible — replace deploy workflow; keep Deployments |
| SSR adapters | Explicitly out of scope (“keep fully static”) |
| Docker | No first-class story; only “serve `dist/`” |
| First-class multi-host templates | None |

Marketing copy still says “anywhere static” / Pages / GitHub Pages while the shipped path is Workers — that mismatch is documentation lag, not a second supported pipeline.

**Bottom line:** Swap CI and keep GitHub Deployments and it works fine. Expect to redo the scaffolded deploy path and lose Workers-specific preview URL niceties unless you recreate them.

content.text:
**No — only the remote “Preview” and “Open live site” links.**

Those two come from GitHub Deployments (`environment_url` on a successful deployment status):

- **PR Preview** → successful deployment for the PR head SHA; no other fallback → missing Deployments means no Preview link.
- **Open live site** → successful deployment for `main` tip first; if missing, still uses Deployments (recent previews) plus `wrangler.toml` worker name to rewrite a Workers preview URL to production. Still no manual/config site URL.

**Local preview is separate.** The in-app preview (`/preview/{id}/` via the daemon/dev server) does not use Deployments at all.

So: Deployments are required for remote published URLs in the UI; day-to-day editing preview is local and independent.

Yes. If their CI creates a GitHub Deployment and sets a successful status with an `http(s)` `environment_url`, Orso will pick it up for Preview (PR head SHA) and Open live site (`main` tip).

Worth keeping in mind:

- Status must be **success**, not just “deployment created.”
- URL must be real `http://` / `https://`.
- Live site looks at the **current `main` tip’s** deployment; older main deploys won’t count if HEAD moved.

The Cloudflare/`wrangler.toml` rewrite is only a fallback when `main` itself has no successful deployment yet. With Deployments set correctly, host choice doesn’t matter.

input.old_string:
## Deploys (Cloudflare Workers)

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds the site and deploys `dist/` to Cloudflare Workers as static
assets (no Worker script; `wrangler.toml` points `[assets]` at `./dist`):

- **Push to `main`** → production deploy (`wrangler deploy`), served at
  `https://<worker>.<subdomain>.workers.dev`. The workflow records a GitHub **deployment**
  for the push commit (`environment: production`) and sets its status to `success` with
  `environment_url` = the live site URL (from wrangler output, or repo variable
  `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` when set).
- **Pull request** (opened, updated, reopened, marked ready) → preview of the PR head commit
  (`wrangler versions upload --preview-alias=<alias>`). The alias comes from the head branch
  (`content/launch-week` → `content-launch-week`), made safe and short enough by
  `.github/scripts/preview-alias.sh`, so every branch keeps one stable preview URL:
  `https://<alias>-<worker>.<subdomain>.workers.dev`. Previews never touch production. The
  workflow then:
  - records a GitHub **deployment** for the PR head commit and sets its status to `success`
    with `environment_url` = the preview URL (or `failure` if the upload failed);
  - posts one **sticky PR comment** with the preview link, updated on every push.

  The CMS orso reads those deployments: a **Preview** link beside the PR status
  ("Draft · Checks pending", "Open · Checks passing", …), and **Open live site** in the
  header when you are on `main`.

### One-time setup

1. Set `name` in `wrangler.toml` to your Worker's name (the first deploy creates it). Keep
   `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` on: preview URLs live on `workers.dev`.
2. In the GitHub repo, **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**:
   - secret `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` — API token with the *Workers Scripts: Edit* permission;
   - secret `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`;
   - variable `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME` (optional; defaults to `astro-marketing`);
   - variable `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` (optional; canonical live origin, e.g. a custom domain — used
     for the production GitHub deployment URL when wrangler’s output is ambiguous).

The job asks for its own token permissions (`contents: read`, `deployments: write`,
`pull-requests: write`); nothing else needs enabling. Pull requests from forks get no secrets,
so they are skipped.

## Deploys

The site is a static `dist/` build. The starter ships Cloudflare Workers CI; any other static
host works the same for orso as long as your workflow records GitHub Deployments (see below).

### What orso needs (any host)

orso’s **Preview** (on a change) and **Open live site** (on `main`) links come only from
GitHub Deployments — not from the host brand. For each successful deploy, create a GitHub
Deployment and set its latest status to `success` with an `http(s)` `environment_url`:

- **PR / change preview** → deployment for the PR **head SHA**, `environment_url` = preview URL
- **Production / live site** → deployment for the current **`main` tip**, `environment_url` = live URL

Without that `environment_url`, those buttons stay empty. Local in-app preview does not use
Deployments.

### Default: Cloudflare Workers

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds the site and deploys `dist/` to Cloudflare Workers as static
assets (no Worker script; `wrangler.toml` points `[assets]` at `./dist`):

- **Push to `main`** → production deploy (`wrangler deploy`), served at
  `https://<worker>.<subdomain>.workers.dev`. The workflow records a GitHub **deployment**
  for the push commit (`environment: production`) and sets its status to `success` with
  `environment_url` = the live site URL (from wrangler output, or repo variable
  `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` when set).
- **Pull request** (opened, updated, reopened, marked ready) → preview of the PR head commit
  (`wrangler versions upload --preview-alias=<alias>`). The alias comes from the head branch
  (`content/launch-week` → `content-launch-week`), made safe and short enough by
  `.github/scripts/preview-alias.sh`, so every branch keeps one stable preview URL:
  `https://<alias>-<worker>.<subdomain>.workers.dev`. Previews never touch production. The
  workflow then:
  - records a GitHub **deployment** for the PR head commit and sets its status to `success`
    with `environment_url` = the preview URL (or `failure` if the upload failed);
  - posts one **sticky PR comment** with the preview link, updated on every push.

### One-time setup (Cloudflare)

1. Set `name` in `wrangler.toml` to your Worker's name (the first deploy creates it). Keep
   `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` on: preview URLs live on `workers.dev`.
2. In the GitHub repo, **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**:
   - secret `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` — API token with the *Workers Scripts: Edit* permission;
   - secret `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`;
   - variable `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME` (optional; defaults to `astro-marketing`);
   - variable `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` (optional; canonical live origin, e.g. a custom domain — used
     for the production GitHub deployment URL when wrangler’s output is ambiguous).

The job asks for its own token permissions (`contents: read`, `deployments: write`,
`pull-requests: write`); nothing else needs enabling. Pull requests from forks get no secrets,
so they are skipped.

### Other hosts

Replace or adapt `deploy.yml` (and drop `wrangler.toml` if unused). Keep the site fully static
(no SSR adapter), build into `dist/`, and keep the Deployments contract above so Preview and
Open live site still work.

Push-and-live on Cloudflare Workers (static assets). `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs `npm ci && npm run build` and deploys `dist/` on every push to `main`, and uploads a preview of every pull request branch at a stable per-branch `workers.dev` URL.

`npm run build` (and thus CI deploy) runs Orso preview checks on the built HTML via `integrations/orso/`: **error**-severity findings fail the build; warnings are logged only. `linkedom` is a production dependency for those checks. When editing the workflow, always record those deployment statuses — without them orso has no URL to link.
